title: Euthanasia, IVF and bioethics
tagline: What the Church teaches about the end of life, assisted suicide, IVF, embryos and stem cells, and how to speak with people who are suffering or caring for someone who is.
whyItMatters: These questions are rarely abstract: they come when someone is dying, cannot conceive or is afraid of being a burden. The Church's teaching is about protecting life and refusing to abandon people.

mindset.tip: Begin with the suffering. People who ask about assisted suicide often fear pain or loneliness. Hear the fear first (Galatians 6:2).
Know the difference between killing and letting die, and between refusing burdensome treatment and refusing care (CCC 2276-2279).
Hear disability advocates who oppose assisted suicide in their own words.
On IVF, be gentle: couples with infertility are carrying a deep grief. Explain the reasons, and show the help the Church supports (CCC 2374-2379).
Send people to qualified help, such as a Catholic bioethics centre, rather than answering a medical question alone.
